Obtain the Horvitz-Thompson direct estimates and standard errors using delta method for a single survey.

Source: R/getDirect.R
getDirect.Rd

Obtain the Horvitz-Thompson direct estimates and standard errors using delta method for a single survey.

Usage

getDirect(
  births,
  years,
  regionVar = "region",
  timeVar = "time",
  clusterVar = "~v001+v002",
  ageVar = "age",
  weightsVar = "v005",
  Ntrials = NULL,
  geo.recode = NULL,
  national.only = FALSE,
  CI = 0.95,
  var.fix = FALSE,
  refStrataVar = NULL
)

Arguments

births

A matrix child-month data from getBirths

years

String vector of the year intervals used

regionVar

Variable name for region in the input births data.

timeVar

Variable name for the time period indicator in the input births data.

clusterVar

Variable name for cluster, typically '~v001 + v002'

ageVar

Variable name for age group. This variable need to be in the form of "a-b" where a and b are both ages in months. For example, "1-11" means age between 1 and 11 months, including both end points. An exception is age less than one month can be represented by "0" or "0-0".

weightsVar

Variable name for sampling weights, typically 'v005'

Ntrials

Variable for the total number of person-months if the input data (births) is in the compact form.

geo.recode

The recode matrix to be used if region name is not consistent across different surveys. See changeRegion.

national.only

Logical indicator to obtain only the national estimates

CI

the desired confidence interval to calculate

var.fix

Logical; if TRUE, we attempt a target-specific synthetic-PSU correction when Rule 2 detects no between-PSU hazard contrast. The default preserves the usual estimates and attributes.

refStrataVar

Optional name of a reference-group column. With NULL, we pool all real observations across areas and sampling strata separately within each period and age band. An explicit column must have one nonmissing value per design stratum within each period. We never infer this column from births$strata.

Value

A data frame of period-region direct estimates, confidence limits, logit estimates, logit variances and precisions, and a survey placeholder. When var.fix = TRUE, we also attach fixed_areas, a character vector of triggered regions (including "All" when triggered), and variance.fix, a data frame with one row per triggered region-period. These attributes include unresolved attempts; fixed_areas does not imply successful correction.

Details

With var.fix = TRUE, we evaluate Rule 2 separately for each area and period. A single real PSU triggers correction. Otherwise, correction requires every exposed PSU's weighted hazard to equal the area's weighted hazard in every exposed age band, within \(10^{-12}\). PSU identities include the sampling stratum, so repeated PSU labels in different strata remain distinct.

We construct references before converting compact death counts to proportions. Within each reference group and period, \(K\) counts all real PSUs with retained exposure, including PSUs without exposure in a particular age band. We average each PSU's exposure-weighted mean sampling weight to obtain \(w^*\). For each age band, synthetic exposure is \(E^*_a = \sum_i w_i E_{ia}/(K w^*)\), and synthetic deaths are \(D^*_a = \sum_i w_i D_{ia}/(K w^*)\). Fractional counts are supported. Observations with missing area labels still contribute to references and national estimates. Zero-exposure rows do not contribute to the correction.

We add one synthetic PSU in each design stratum present in a triggered target, using that stratum's reference group. We augment a separate full-survey design for each target before subsetting it and applying the existing estimator. We retain the original design for untriggered targets and treat the national estimate as its own target. Thus, another area's synthetic PSUs cannot change an untriggered estimate or its variance. The correction can change both the point estimate and variance. Simple named multistage cluster formulas, such as ~psu + household, are supported in the correction path.

We retain the zero-death guard after augmentation. Targets without data remain missing, and degenerate references need not produce positive variance. We do not impose a variance floor or pool reference periods. The audit has character columns region, years, status, reason, trigger, and reference.groups; integer counts real.psus, phantom.psus, and phantom.rows; and numeric totals phantom.weighted.deaths and phantom.weighted.exposure. We label an attempt "fixed" only when the augmented target no longer satisfies Rule 2 and has a finite logit estimate and finite positive variance. Otherwise, we label it "unresolved" and record the reason. Empty trigger and audit attributes retain the same types and columns.

References

Li, Z., Hsiao, Y., Godwin, J., Martin, B. D., Wakefield, J., Clark, S. J., & with support from the United Nations Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation and its technical advisory group. (2019). Changes in the spatial distribution of the under-five mortality rate: Small-area analysis of 122 DHS surveys in 262 subregions of 35 countries in Africa. PloS one, 14(1), e0210645.

Mercer, L. D., Wakefield, J., Pantazis, A., Lutambi, A. M., Masanja, H., & Clark, S. (2015). Space-time smoothing of complex survey data: small area estimation for child mortality. The annals of applied statistics, 9(4), 1889.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(DemoData)
years <- c("85-89", "90-94", "95-99", "00-04", "05-09", "10-14")
mean <- getDirect(births = DemoData[[1]],  years = years, 
regionVar = "region", timeVar = "time", clusterVar = "~clustid+id", 
ageVar = "age", weightsVar = "weights", geo.recode = NULL)
} # }
